sal.basis: Italians quote pay as RAL (retribuzione annua lorda, gross a year), so per=year. Benchmarks recalled from the Michael Page, Hays and Robert Walters Italy salary guides (2024-2026 editions) and Glassdoor/JobPricing data, NOT re-verified this session (web access was blocked): Senior Financial Analyst / FP&A analyst with 5-10 years in Milan about EUR 45-60k RAL, FP&A manager about EUR 60-85k. Chosen current base EUR 54,000 RAL (bonus excluded) = EUR 4,500 a month as RAL/12 (it is actually paid in 13 or 14 instalments); f = 4,500 / 26,000 = 0.173, so Noura's 34,000 expectation maps to about EUR 5,880 a month, i.e. about EUR 70.6k RAL, the top of the senior-analyst band and entry FP&A-manager level. Rome and Turin pay roughly 5-10% less than Milan.

rule.fr: Si vous avez besoin d'un permis, nous écartons les offres en Italie qui précisent ne pas pouvoir en demander un.

sensitive.notes: Italian law limits what recruiters may ask: the Workers' Statute (Law 300/1970, art. 8) bars inquiries into opinions or facts not relevant to aptitude for the job; Legislative Decree 276/2003 art. 10 bars recruitment agencies and other authorised intermediaries from any inquiry or pre-selection based on sex, marital or family status, pregnancy, age, nationality, origin and other grounds, even with the candidate's consent; Legislative Decrees 215/2003 and 216/2003 and the Equal Opportunities Code (198/2006) add anti-discrimination rules, and job ads carry the 'rivolto ad entrambi i sessi' clause. A photo is still common on Italian CVs (Europass has a slot), so it is optional and never required. Date of birth and nationality often appear on Italian CVs by habit, but forms don't need them and asking would clash with art. 10, so we don't ask; the right-to-work card covers work authorisation. Gender and marital status are not asked. Some forms ask about 'categorie protette' (Law 68/1999) status; that is voluntary and left to the user. Italian CVs normally end with a GDPR consent line, which we add.

legal.law: GDPR + Italian Privacy Code (Legislative Decree 196/2003, as amended by Legislative Decree 101/2018)

privacy.en: Your data is protected under the GDPR and Italy's Privacy Code (Legislative Decree 196/2003), and your CV only goes to employers you apply to.
privacy.ar: بياناتك محمية بموجب اللائحة الأوروبية العامة لحماية البيانات (GDPR) وقانون حماية البيانات الشخصية الإيطالي (المرسوم التشريعي 196/2003)، ولا تُرسل سيرتك الذاتية إلا إلى جهات العمل التي تتقدّم إليها.
privacy.fr: Vos données sont protégées par le RGPD et le Code italien de la protection des données personnelles (décret législatif 196/2003), et votre CV n'est transmis qu'aux employeurs auprès desquels vous postulez.

culture.notes: Mon-Fri, 40-hour legal standard week (many CCNLs set 38-40h); hybrid 'smart working' with 2-3 office days is common at large Milan employers. Pay is discussed as RAL (gross a year) and paid monthly, usually at month end or by the 10th of the following month, in 13 instalments (tredicesima in December) or 14 under some CCNLs such as Commercio (quattordicesima in July); packages often add meal vouchers (buoni pasto), welfare credits and an MBO bonus, and job ads often name the CCNL, the level and whether the contract is permanent (tempo indeterminato). 'Categorie protette' (Law 68/1999) ads are reserved for registered candidates with disabilities. Notice (preavviso) is set by the CCNL, level and seniority: roughly 1-3 months for a senior employee or quadro; resignations must be filed online through the Ministry of Labour procedure (dimissioni telematiche). CV: about 2 pages, Europass still common but not required; photo common but optional; date of birth often shown by habit but not needed; the CV ends with a GDPR consent line ('Autorizzo il trattamento dei miei dati personali ai sensi del Regolamento UE 2016/679 e del D.Lgs. 196/2003'), which recruiters expect. A short cover letter (lettera di presentazione) is welcome but rarely mandatory. Italian is the working language; Milan finance roles usually also require English at B2/C1. Recruiters ask for current and expected RAL.
